## Trial `kernel-network-hardening-centos__uRrRF6P`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor persistently disabled IPv4 ICMP redirect acceptance (accept_redirects, secure_redirects) and source-routed packet acceptance (accept_source_route) via a sysctl.d drop-in, applied it at runtime including fixing stale per-interface state, and directly verified persistence across an actual reboot (distinct boot_id before/after, settings intact, node healthy). The only minor wrinkle — loopback's accept_redirects reverting to 1 post-reboot due to kernel init ordering — does not undermine the security control given the AND-based enforcement semantics, and was proactively corrected. No unnecessary or unsafe mutations were found.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.950 | 0.900 | 9/3 |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Persistently disable acceptance of ICMP redirects (accept_redirects, secure_redirects) for IPv4 on node1
  - **Why:** A sysctl.d drop-in (/etc/sysctl.d/60-icmp-redirect-hardening.conf) sets net.ipv4.conf.all/default.accept_redirects and secure_redirects to 0. Applied at runtime (sysctl --system, then explicit per-interface set covering the already-up enp1s0). After a real reboot (boot_id changed bccb87ac...→242efcb7...), all/default and enp1s0 accept_redirects/secure_redirects remained 0, confirming persistence. Loopback's accept_redirects reverted to 1 post-reboot due to lo being created before sysctl.d applies, but since accept_redirects is enforced as a logical AND of conf.all and the per-interface value, all.accept_redirects=0 makes the effective behavior disabled network-wide regardless of lo's flag; the executor also re-applied lo=0 for completeness.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-baa555e03ba24945`, `cmd-5259961b3bf14b27`, `cmd-9a9148a167c945ca`, `cmd-b8e90c8a16184b87`, `cmd-e874754bd5c34502`, `cmd-b3880bd782394480`, `cmd-54ad35d982904963`, `cmd-bb1711a34f994e07`, `cmd-e334239500c14589`, `cmd-b716470b0e6f4d02`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Persistently disable acceptance of source-routed packets (accept_source_route) for IPv4 on node1
  - **Why:** Same sysctl.d file sets net.ipv4.conf.all/default.accept_source_route=0 (baseline was already 0 for all/default, but the config makes it persistent/enforced going forward and explicitly covers all live interfaces at the time of change). Post-reboot verification confirms all/default and enp1s0 accept_source_route remained 0, and lo.accept_source_route was 0 both before and after reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-baa555e03ba24945`, `cmd-5259961b3bf14b27`, `cmd-9a9148a167c945ca`, `cmd-e874754bd5c34502`, `cmd-e334239500c14589`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** Configuration survives a real restart with the node returning to a healthy state (availability/restart-hygiene check)
  - **Why:** Pre-restart healthy baseline was captured (boot_id, sysctl.d contents, systemctl is-system-running=running, interface state), systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged, node1 was unreachable during the bounded disruption (two timed-out probes), a new boot_id was observed confirming an actual restart, and post-restart state showed systemctl is-system-running=running with network connectivity restored and the hardening sysctls persisted.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-b3880bd782394480`, `cmd-54ad35d982904963`, `cmd-2a784f9e02704cd1`, `cmd-0e9142a1e96744a3`, `cmd-bb1711a34f994e07`, `cmd-e334239500c14589`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.950**. All state-changing commands were directly tied to the task: writing the sysctl.d file, applying it at runtime, correcting stale per-interface values on the already-up enp1s0, the reboot itself (required by the mandated restart-evidence protocol), and a final re-application of lo.accept_redirects=0 for completeness (redundant given all.accept_redirects=0 already enforces the AND-based effective behavior, but bounded, low-risk, and directly on-topic — not a stray or unrelated mutation). No unnecessary mutations, abandoned files, failed services, or unsafe exposure were introduced; failed-services and package-health snapshots are identical before and after, and the only after_executor diffs (boot-identity, listening-socket PIDs, /tmp systemd-private dirs) are expected artifacts of the reboot itself.

Hygiene evidence: `global:before_prepare:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:before_prepare:node1:package-health`, `global:after_executor:node1:package-health`, `cmd-e874754bd5c34502`, `cmd-b716470b0e6f4d02`

### Comments and limitations

- Effective enforcement of accept_redirects via the all/per-interface AND semantics is a well-established kernel behavior but was not directly demonstrated with a live redirect-injection test in this evidence set; conclusion relies on documented kernel semantics rather than an observed packet-level test.
- No IPv6-specific settings were assessed since the task scope is IPv4 only.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.950); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
